missing_information_flags.question: What are the names and email addresses of the 82 employees, and what is the correct email domain? The headcount export is stuck with the PEO. Every address in this configuration is recorded as N/A because the packet contains none.

Is the February travel arrangement still in effect, or does Leo Novak's all-travel rule replace it? Dev Batra asked exactly this in the channel on 2026-07-30 and received no answer. See the conflicts section — this is the single most consequential open item in the packet.
Which employees are managers? The 50% uplift for GTM and ops managers cannot be applied to anyone until managers are identified.
What are the individual executive limits? Roughly five people are affected and the packet states these are handled case by case.

Can Stan Pollard both own the software card and be restricted from touching limits? The Ramp role that grants user administration without spend authority also prevents holding a card or seeing spend, so the two requests cannot both be met by one role. See the conflicts section.
What monthly limit should the travel programme carry, and who holds travel cards? The packet states travel is a separate programme still being designed.
What is the full name of the Sales lead, recorded here under the handle jj?
Who holds the offsite card? Dev Batra owns offsite logistics, but the packet does not say whether the budget sits with one person or is shared across the organisers.
Should a receipt threshold and a memo threshold be configured? Neither is mentioned anywhere in this packet.
Which cardholders need physical cards rather than virtual ones, and what are the shipping addresses? Card format is never discussed in this packet.

Has the employee who left in January been removed from the shared Amex card? The February notes record four people sharing one card number, one of whom had already left. That card is outside Ramp, but the exposure is live until it is cancelled.
Should meals be reimbursed on a per diem or on actuals? The February notes park this and record that no proposal followed.

Should the software card also cover cloud infrastructure — AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and similar? The packet describes software subscriptions only, so infrastructure is currently excluded and would decline. With 340 vendors and a $30,000 monthly budget this is worth confirming before the first billing cycle.
Should the November offsite budget accept reimbursement claims as well as card spend? The packet describes it as a card budget only, so reimbursements are switched off.

conflicts.description: Travel approvals. The February planning meeting agreed a tiered arrangement in which travel under $2,500 is auto-approved by a department manager; a later message from the CEO requires every travel transaction to route to the CEO. This is the most consequential open item in the packet, and it is not settled by recency: the earlier source records an agreement the CEO himself made, the note-taker states plainly that no confirmation or cancellation of that trial could be found, the June meeting that would have decided it was cancelled and never rescheduled, and when the VP Ops asked in the channel whether the two were compatible the question received no reply.
conflicts.source_a: fragmented_notes_feb2026.md, line 19 — recording what the February planning meeting agreed: "leo agreed to try the $2,500 threshold for Q2"
conflicts.source_b: slack_export_finance.txt — Leo Novak (CEO), [2026-07-30 08:55], requiring every travel transaction to route to the CEO: "ALL travel needs my direct approval until further notice"
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded the all-travel rule, as the most recent instruction, from the CEO, phrased as standing until further notice. It is provisional only. Applying it silently would reverse an agreement the CEO made in February without anyone confirming that reversal was intended, and would reinstate the single-approver bottleneck the February meeting existed to remove. Raised as blocking: this needs an explicit answer from Leo Novak before go-live, not an inference.

conflicts.description: Whether Stan Pollard can both own the software card and be barred from changing limits. Both requests are reasonable and cannot both be satisfied by one Ramp role: the role granting user administration without spend authority also removes the ability to hold a card or view spend, and any role able to hold a $30,000 monthly card can also see spend.
conflicts.source_a: slack_export_finance.txt — Stan Pollard (IT), [2026-07-29 10:06], claiming ownership of the software card: "owned by me specifically. i want to see every subscription with my own eyes"
conflicts.source_b: slack_export_finance.txt — Rachel Kim (Head of Finance), [2026-08-04 10:12], restricting the same person from changing limits: "stan does user onboarding/offboarding ONLY — he should not be able to touch limits"
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded Stan Pollard in the user-administration role, which satisfies the stated restriction, and left the software card unassigned. This is the safer of the two readings because the restriction was stated by the Head of Finance about someone else's access, while the ownership claim was that person describing a personal preference. The alternative — a spending role for Stan Pollard plus a separate person for user administration — is equally available and needs Hypergrowth Inc. to choose.

conflicts.description: The offsite budget. The February notes record an estimate of $50,000 to $60,000, explicitly a guess; the later channel message states $60,000 as a total.
conflicts.source_a: fragmented_notes_feb2026.md, line 29 — recording an early estimate of the offsite budget: "budget TBD (rachel guessing $50-60k)"
conflicts.source_b: slack_export_finance.txt — Dev Batra (VP Ops), [2026-07-31 14:31], fixing the offsite budget: "$60k total, expires after the offsite"

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Every travel transaction approved by Leo Novak personally, and the February alternative of manager approval below $2,500 with escalation above it.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp has no endpoint for creating approval policies. Both arrangements are recorded in this configuration as desired state, and whichever Hypergrowth Inc. confirms has to be built in the Ramp application before go-live.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — no approval-policy write endpoint; only /blank-canvas-approvals/* (acts on existing instances) and GET /spend-programs/{id}/workflow-nodes (read-only); zero approval OAuth scopes. support.ramp.com 'Set up your spend approval policies', checked 2026-08-30 — tiered approval chains ARE configurable in Ramp's in-app approvals workflow builder, so this is a UI-only capability rather than a missing one.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Tiered approval chains are a standard Ramp feature, but are built in the approvals workflow builder inside the Ramp application rather than through the API. The tier structure requested is recorded here as desired state, and the deployment owner recreates it in Ramp before go-live. Routing by amount and by user role is available on every plan; more elaborate conditions require Ramp Plus, so confirm the plan tier first.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Leo Novak to be told about any card carrying more than $10,000 a month.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: This is a request to be informed rather than a spending rule, and Ramp has no notification configuration surface. No card in this configuration currently exceeds $10,000 a month, so nothing would trigger it today; the software programme at $30,000 a month is a programme budget rather than a personal card.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — no notifications resource; nearest primitive is POST /webhooks (transaction events), which delivers events but does not evaluate threshold or routing rules.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp has no rule engine for routing spend alerts to a chat channel or to a named person. Ramp's Slack integration, switched on by the deployment owner in the Ramp application, covers the common case of posting card activity to a channel; anything conditional, such as alerting only above a set monthly amount, needs a webhook subscription with the threshold applied by the receiving system.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: One limit per department covering its individual contributors, at $750 for engineering, $2,500 for GTM and $1,000 for ops.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp limits belong to one person, so each department limit becomes one limit per employee. With no roster, the counts are the approximate figures given in the channel rather than a list of people.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — POST /funds requires a single user_id, so a group limit becomes one fund per member; is_shareable with /funds/{id}/members is the nearest shared-pool primitive and has different semantics (one shared pot, not N).
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp attaches a spend limit to one person at a time, so a limit described for a team becomes either a separate limit of that size for each member or a single shared pot the whole team draws down. Those are materially different outcomes and the wording of a request rarely settles which is meant, so the deployment owner should confirm the intent for each team-level limit before setup.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Onboarding 82 employees once the roster arrives from the PEO.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp creates users one at a time rather than from a file. At 82 people this is a loop rather than an obstacle, but it is worth stating plainly since the roster is expected to arrive as a single export.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — no bulk user endpoint; POST /users/deferred is per-user and async (poll /users/deferred/status/{task_id}), with idempotency_key required in the body.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp has no bulk user import: people are created one at a time and each creation is processed in the background. At the volumes described this is not a practical constraint, since the roster is loaded in a single automated pass rather than typed in, and each request carries a duplicate-protection key so a re-run of a weekly wave cannot create the same person twice.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Cards for 82 employees across four departments.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp creates virtual cards as part of issuing a spend limit rather than on request, and physical cards need a shipping address for each holder. Card format is never discussed in this packet, so nothing physical is specified.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — POST /cards/physical exists (requires shipping_address and user_id) but virtual cards are GET-only and are issued via funds rather than created directly.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Both card types are available: a virtual card is issued alongside a spend limit, while a physical card is ordered explicitly and needs a shipping address for each recipient. Shipping addresses are not present in the material provided, so the deployment owner supplies one per physical cardholder before those cards can be ordered.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Adjusting the software programme as the 340 vendor subscriptions consolidate, which the packet expects to happen.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp spend programmes cannot be edited through the API once created. The software budget is explicitly expected to fall over time, so this programme in particular should be reviewed before it is created.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — /spend-programs has GET and POST only and /spend-programs/{id} is GET-only; there is no PATCH or DELETE, so programs are immutable via the API.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: A spend program cannot be edited through the API once created; later changes are made in the Ramp application instead. That makes the review of program definitions before go-live the cheapest point to change anything, and the deployment owner should treat it as the moment to settle names, limits and restrictions.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Distinct permission levels for a CEO, a Head of Finance, a VP Ops, an executive assistant acting as administrator, an IT lead restricted to user management, and a Sales lead.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp offers a fixed set of roles with no seniority or scoping dimension, so each role here is matched to the closest available one. Every non-obvious match is listed in the assumptions above, and one of those matches cannot be satisfied at all — see the conflict regarding Stan Pollard.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) plus support.ramp.com 'User roles overview', checked 2026-08-30 — Ramp exposes six assignable roles with fixed, documented permission sets and no seniority or scoping dimension, so mapping customer job titles onto Ramp roles is a per-person judgement call.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp offers a fixed set of six assignable roles with defined permissions and no seniority or scoping dimension, so each job title is matched to the closest role by judgement rather than by rule. Every non-obvious match is recorded with the job title, the role chosen, and what that role can see and do, for the deployment owner to confirm before invitations go out.
